task: Task B - what information does each depth representation actually carry

inputs.sampler: scripts/sensor_dataset.py imported directly (corridor addresses, bilinear depth, d0 rule, sec channel)

scale.corridor_subsample: every 2nd route, every 2nd station, every 2nd lateral; arena-edge points |x| or |y| > 39.5 m dropped

part1_algebra.verdict_algebra: CONFIRMED: undetermined without d_0 unless s_i = s_0
part1_algebra.verdict_in_practice: REFUTED as a material loss, because s_0 is itself in the D tensor (ray_sec1 at cell [0,16]) and pins d_0

verified_example_pair_f104.identical_D_cell_input: delta_d differs by 8 mm, sec by 1.5e-4
verified_example_pair_f104.resolved_by: start sec 1.0223 vs 1.0709 (both present in the same tensor at cell [0,16])

part2_d0.decomposition: d0 = (H - z0) sec(theta0); start heights z0 have std 0.18-0.38 m, so the spread of d0 is essentially the spread of sec(theta0)
part2_d0.histogram: counts per 0.5 m bin in shift.json -> d0_histogram; figure d0_histogram.png

part3_recoverability.target: z - z0 (the quantity the deployed height channel carries); fit on f104 groups only

closed_forms.b_and_c_and_d: z = H - d/sec exactly; RMSE 0.0 m on every arena
closed_forms.a_plus_one_constant: z - z0 = Qbar (1 - sec0/sec) - dd/sec with Qbar = 109.953 m fitted on f104: RMSE 0.0047 m on f104 held out, 0.0045-0.0081 m on the five unseen arenas

local_slope_decode_with_one_plugin_const.form: dz/dl = -(1/s) d(depth_rel)/dl + ((D + depth_rel)/s^2) d(sec)/dl, D = 115.211 m fitted on f104

part3_recoverability.architecture_note: scripts/gen_riskmodel.Net: four 3x3 convolutions (receptive field 9 stations) then f.mean(-1)/f.amax(-1) collapse the lateral axis before the BiGRU runs along stations, so the start cell's sec cannot reach a distant station until after the lateral profile has been pooled

verdict.missing_information: ruled out at the 1 cm level: the delivered D tensor determines z - z0 to 4.5-12 mm on all six arenas
verdict.harder_transform: supported and quantified: the required correction is 1.9-2.5x larger than the signal it hides, needs a 110:1 weight against a channel 148x smaller in scale, and the height offset term needs the route-start cell, which the CNN front end cannot reach before it pools the lateral axis
verdict.cross_arena_shift: real but second order for the D channels themselves (AUC 0.63-0.72, 0.2-7.1% unseen cells) versus height (AUC 0.56, 0.01-0.1%); it matters because a partly-learned correction leaves a position-dependent residual that is deterministic on one static training arena
verdict.not_tested_here: no trained checkpoint was probed and no closed-loop run was made; these are representational measurements, not a measurement of what the D checkpoint computes
